Prevent the 3pm sugar crash👇🏽

Most of the snacks marketed to families are designed to be grabbed fast and eaten faster.

The problem is they spike blood sugar, wear off in an hour, and leave kids irritable, distracted, and asking for something else ten minutes later.

These are the swaps we actually use in our house. Real food, naturally sweet, and easy enough to throw together on a Tuesday morning before school.

🐜 Ants on a log: celery sticks spread with peanut butter and topped with raisins. Done in two minutes. (Or make my "reindeer" version if your kids get bored of ants on a log!)
🍿 Creative homemade popcorn - add any toppings you like! My kids love just a little bit of caramel or sugar to make "kettle corn" but you really don't need a lot to add sweetness. 1 tsp is enough!
🍎 Apple slices with Peanut or Greek yogurt dip: slice an apple, mix plain Greek yogurt with a tiny drizzle of honey and a pinch of cinnamon. That's it. You can also do this with peanut butter mixed with a tiny drizzle of honey for sweetness.
🌰 Energy bites: Take rolled oats + any nut butter + any toppings your kids like (my kids like dried fruit + chocolate chips). Roll them into balls, chill in the fridge, enjoy all week!
🥣 Yogurt bowls: Better than fro-yo! My kids love Greek yogurt topped with berries, granola, nut butter and a drizzle of honey. 
🫐 Blueberry cobbler: frozen blueberries microwaved for 60 seconds, topped with a handful of oats, a drizzle of maple syrup, and a pinch of cinnamon. Feels like dessert, works as a snack.

Same fun. A fraction of the sugar.

And the kind of snack that actually keeps kids full until the next meal.

You don't have to be a plant-based family to make these work for yours.
